expectations.text: Presents all three guardrail architectures - single break-even floor, tiered ladder, and portfolio with ring-fenced exploration - before drafting numbers.
expectations.evidence: "Normal ranking (efficiency: tiered ladder > single floor > portfolio; effort: single floor > ladder > portfolio) would put the portfolio model last on cost." — all three named before the numeric policy is drafted.

expectations.text: States the ranking out loud across axes (efficiency, value in false stops avoided and learning kept, effort) rather than presenting one option.
expectations.evidence: Only two axes are explicitly ranked ("efficiency: tiered ladder > single floor > portfolio; effort: single floor > ladder > portfolio"); a "value" axis (false stops avoided / learning kept) is never named as a ranked axis.

expectations.text: Promotes the portfolio model above its default rank because the efficiency bar has already strangled testing.
expectations.evidence: "an efficiency bar has already strangled testing' (your media buyer's complaint, literally), the portfolio model is promoted above its default rank."

expectations.text: Uses the in-house analyst who already tracks marginal returns to argue the portfolio model's effort cost collapses for this account.
expectations.evidence: "Your analyst already tracking marginal returns weekly is precisely that asset... you're not standing up new capability, just pointing existing capability at a carved-out budget."

expectations.text: Ring-fences an exploration budget as a declared share of spend with its own separate kill rules, exempt from the main floor.
expectations.evidence: "Size 10-15% of the $85K core = $8,500-$12,750/month, ring-fenced, NOT counted against the core MER floor"

expectations.text: Gives exploration tests spend-based judgment rules (hypothesis, decision date, spend cap) instead of the production 2.8x bar.
expectations.evidence: "Rule spend-based evidence gate, not a ROAS floor: no kill before $1,000-$1,500 spent per new channel/audience AND 14 days live... Decision at the gate: keep... extend... or cut"

expectations.text: Names the failure mode explicitly: testing held to the production efficiency bar quietly stops testing.
expectations.evidence: "No separation between proven and exploratory spend. New channels/audiences are held to the same bar as your scaled Meta/Google core, which is exactly backwards"

expectations.text: Asks where the 2.8x figure came from and re-derives break-even from the business's own margin, asking for the margin if unknown, rather than keeping 2.8x unexamined.
expectations.evidence: "your existing 2.8x bar implies a break-even contribution margin of 1 ÷ 2.8 = 35.7% ... Confirm which — if your real CM3 is higher, 2.8x has been over-tight this whole time; if lower, you've been losing money"

expectations.text: Flags that one flat threshold across all channels and audiences starves prospecting, which always looks worse than retargeting.
expectations.evidence: The three named faults (no evidence gate, no separation of proven/exploratory, blended-only measurement) do not include an explicit statement that a flat threshold structurally starves prospecting versus retargeting.

expectations.text: Waits for the user's choice of architecture rather than unilaterally imposing one.
expectations.evidence: "Recommendation: run both, on different pools of spend" is delivered as a decided recommendation, and "What to do next" gives direct action steps rather than awaiting the user's architecture choice.

expectations.text: Asks whether the mandate is a one-off fix or a compounding asset, and what effort ceiling exists for a standing review, before or while ranking.
expectations.evidence: No such question appears; the analyst's existing weekly cadence is simply assumed as the standing-review capacity.

expectations.text: Pairs whatever efficiency guardrail replaces the 2.8x bar with a counter-metric that exposes gaming.
expectations.evidence: "Blended MER... counter-metric: new-customer share of orders" and "Contribution margin after ads... counter-metric: discount depth"
